The repeal starts taxable years after December 31, 2025; the status changes use taxable years after December 31, 2026 versus conforming PLAN YEARS on/after January 1, 2027. Senate lacks those direct conforming deletions/renumbering; application of the retained reference to deleted 36B(c)(1)(B) remains RESERVED. The 5000A(d)(3) reference change does not amend the existing zero monetary penalty components. No actual award, revived penalty, whole-package closure or component preference follows.

Exchange verification concerns INDIVIDUAL CREDIT COVERAGE MONTHS, not an enrollment ban: failure of this paragraph ALONE does NOT make an individual ineligible to enroll. Applicant PROVIDED OR VERIFIED information applies TO THE EXTENT RELEVANT. Senate requires enrollment AND advance-credit verification, with NO House cost-sharing third prong, HOUSEHOLD INCOME AND FAMILY SIZE and WHETHER AN ELIGIBLE ALIEN. Past-month verification prints IF. Secretary MAY waive ONLY (A) for one or more tax-year months enrolled during an SEP BASED ON CHANGE IN OWN FAMILY SIZE. ANY available data AND RELIABLE third-party sources remain FOR VERIFICATION BY THE APPLICANT. Exact June 25, 2025 final-rule(iii), printed 2026 ONLY, is expressly applied as though to ALL PLAN YEARS AFTER 2025; no substitution of its separate two-year introductory baseline or House March proposal. Both filing-compliance references retain HHS notification, advances for filer OR married spouse, the relevant tax-data year and failure to file/reconcile, with direct filer failure notice OR protected indirect risk/education notice; not a test imposed without those predicates or guaranteed notice-to-loss interval. ANY APPLICANT MAY use an Exchange-provided process BEGINNING NOT LATER THAN AUGUST 1 for the SUBSEQUENT PLAN YEAR; not a universal applicant deadline. Senate process covers HOUSEHOLD INCOME AND ENROLLMENT. Sections 112201/71303 apply to TAXABLE YEARS BEGINNING AFTER DECEMBER 31, 2027, distinct from the House discrepancy PLAN YEARS ON/AFTER JANUARY 1, 2026 and the Senate incorporated-rule duration. No automatic credit/coverage outcome, whole-package closure or component preference is inferred.

Senate cost-sharing dependency is now source-complete for this bounded question; no House annual filing/extension amendment or notice-version substitution is imported. NO reduction for ANY MONTH UNLESS a COVERAGE MONTH FOR WHICH 36B CREDIT IS ALLOWED TO THE INSURED OR AN APPLICABLE TAXPAYER ON THE INSURED'S BEHALF: necessary, not sufficient, and not every insured personally filing. Definitions share 36B terms; data use ADVANCE-DETERMINATION TAX YEAR, not credit-allowed tax year. The undeleted cost-sharing sentence/basic-health branch alone does not establish continuing benefits. Question 34 remains RESERVED, without actual credit/reduction/basic-health award or loss, legal repair, full-package closure or acceptance.

Senate tax is 1 percent and concerns only the named physical funding, subject to separate nonapplication alternatives. One alternative requires funds withdrawn from an account held in or by an institution described in (A)-(H); that institution must also be subject to BSA chapter 53/subchapter II. The other alternative requires funding with a US-issued debit or credit card. No any-bank/card exception or universal cash charge. WITHOUT REGARD TO debit (B) is not automatic exclusion of every prepaid card. No House citizen-verification/36C/6050BB mechanism is imported or a citizenship-based Senate exemption inferred. Both retain consumer/NATURAL-PERSON sender in a DEFINED STATE, provider-initiated ELECTRONIC transfer to FOREIGN designated recipient, account-independence, normal-course provider and SMALL-VALUE exclusion. Physical funding is distinct from electronic transfer technology. SENDER pays; provider COLLECTS FROM SENDER AND REMITS QUARTERLY; secondary liability ONLY unpaid-at-transfer AND uncollected extent. Transfers apply AFTER DECEMBER 31, 2025. Anti-conduit deeming/regulatory discretion is not observed avoidance, wrongdoing or an individual tax finding. No specific person, provider, transaction path, credit/refund or actual net-cost outcome is determined.

Selected Senate 71301/71302/71303 retain own eligible-alien/income/verification predicates and effective dates; these sections do not contain House named-memo amendments. No House title-wide/CSR-section/Federal-payment-sentence exclusion is imported, and no automatic DACA eligibility or whole-package absence of DACA effects is inferred. Original memo is historical context, not a current ACA eligibility decision.

The qualifying child's defined SSN is required in either case. The Senate also requires the taxpayer's defined SSN or, on a joint return, the defined SSN of at least one spouse. This is not both spouses on every joint return or a child number alone. No House SIMILAR 32(d) is imported. Own $2,200 context and after-2025 credit inflation; The senior mechanism in 70103 is addressed separately below. Both child-credit amendments begin with TAXABLE YEARS BEGINNING AFTER DECEMBER 31, 2024. The defined SSN may be issued to either a US citizen or an individual under the named work-authorized-alien branch. In either case, it must have been issued before the due date for the return. Any SSA number, an ITIN or citizenship proof alone is insufficient. Complete 24/152 retain own qualifying-child, NOT-ATTAINED-17, citizenship/residence/adoption, relationship/support/abode/joint-return/tie/custody and other exceptions, income/refundable/identification/year limits. Existing 24(h)(4)(C) PARAGRAPH (7) fallback is RETAINED but new claimant/spouse-failure application RESERVED as question 39: no guaranteed $500 or whole-family loss. Zero-exemption reference rule does not itself eliminate credit. Mathematical-error scope changes to SECTION 24; own alleged-error/explanation notice, no petition BASED ON THAT NOTICE, abatement request WITHIN 60 DAYS AFTER NOTICE SENT, mandatory abatement UPON RECEIPT, deficiency reassessment and collection stay remain. No actual fraud, debt, indexed payment, credit/refund, every-remedy loss or individual/tax-family determination.

The Senate $6,000 deduction is per qualified person. The listed alternatives are the taxpayer or the spouse on a joint return. In either case, the claimed person must have attained 65 before the tax year closes and must supply that person's defined SSN. One spouse's number does not establish deductions for both. The phaseout rate is 6 percent over $75,000, or $150,000 on a joint return. A taxpayer married within section 7703 must file jointly with the spouse; the new House similar-32(d) clause, blind bonus and hypothetical-itemizer mechanism are not imported. Own mathematical-error label is (W). The same-version SSN definition permits issuance to either a US citizen or the named work-authorized-alien category. In either case, the number must have been issued before the due date for the return. Other SSA numbers or ITINs do not alone qualify. Child-credit identification is not senior identification. Own taxable-income, itemization, spouse/exemption and marital predicates remain, along with the nonresident-alien standard-deduction exclusion, without an individual eligibility finding or accepted override. A deduction is not a dollar-for-dollar credit, exemption of all Social Security income or guaranteed refund. Both senior amendments apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024; their own upper limit is a taxable year beginning before January 1, 2029. Modified income includes the named 911/931/933 exclusions. Mathematical-error notice requires the alleged error and explanation; the no-petition rule concerns that notice. The abatement request period is 60 days after notice is sent, abatement follows receipt, reassessment uses deficiency procedures and collection is stayed during the abatement period. No actual debt, fraud, payment or loss of every remedy.

Senate requires the individual's defined SSN in all cases. A credit for the qualified expenses of an individual other than the taxpayer or spouse must also include that individual's name and defined SSN. No new House spouse-number or similar-32(d) amendment is imported; retained 25A(g)(6) requires joint filing for a taxpayer married within 7703. No separate-return eligibility or child-credit joint-number alternative is inferred. The same-version defined SSN permits citizen issuance or the named work-authorized-alien branch. In either case, issuance must precede the return due date; an ITIN or any SSA number does not alone suffice. The old AOTC student on-or-before deadline is distinct. The institution EIN clause is AOTC-only and tied to the named taxpayer-paid qualified expenses taken into account, with retained dependent-payment treatment; it is not a Lifetime Learning or every-institution requirement. Full credit, income, student, institution, qualified-expense, assistance, dependent, prepayment, double-benefit, payee-statement, refund and recapture conditions remain, without an individual amount or eligibility determination. The AOTC student reference freezes HEA 484(a)(1), with its own exceptions, at August 5, 1997; it does not import all current student eligibility or its citizenship paragraph. The institution definition retains frozen HEA 481 and its own title IV eligibility condition. Exact historical passages and amendment chronology are bound; full HEA 481 comparison uses two declared split-word normalizations, without source mutation or personal/institution classification. A taxpayer nonresident during any portion of the year retains the conditional 6013(g)/(h) chapter-1 resident-election path, each with own spouse/status/both-election and duration/termination/re-election predicates; this is not all-noncitizen denial or immigration status/work authorization. Both apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025. Own mathematical-error (J) changes TIN to SSN or EIN; alleged-error/explanation notice, 60 days after notice is sent, abatement upon receipt, deficiency reassessment and collection stay remain. No debt, wrongdoing, guaranteed credit/refund, loss of every remedy or whole-package closure.

Senate 100052(8) family-unity funding uses a purpose within the $29.85 billion additional fiscal year 2025 ICE account, available through September 30, 2029; neither the full envelope nor House $20 million is a separate Senate family earmark. Pending specified charge, charged only with the INA 275(a) misdemeanor and entry with the alien's under-18 child all retain their own scope; care/custody expressly in accordance with applicable laws, plus co-detention purpose. Charge is not guilt or an actual custody result. Accompanied parent/child is not UAC; no House child-disclosure/withdrawal mechanism, universal detention or family entitlement imported. No individual outcome, legal-constraint adjudication or full-package closure.

Senate 100052 uses one additional fiscal year 2025 $29.85 billion ICE envelope through September 30, 2029 for listed purposes; no House account amounts or hiring minima imported. Hiring/training includes named investigators and retired hiring priority; recruitment/onboarding distinct. The Director may provide a performance bonus to a named ICE agent, officer or attorney who demonstrates exemplary service. The Director may provide a retention bonus to a named ICE agent, officer or attorney who commits to two additional years of immigration-enforcement service. The Director may provide a signing bonus to a named ICE agent, officer or attorney only if that person is hired on or after enactment and commits to five years of immigration-enforcement service. Signing is may, unlike House shall. For retention and signing bonuses, the Director shall provide each qualifying individual a written service agreement with its required period, amount, payment and early-termination terms. Transportation/related departure-removal costs, IT including fee collection, facilities/fleet, 287(g) agreements, VOICE staffing/nonfinancial victim assistance and OPLA immigration-enforcement/removal representation remain distinct purposes. Full material 287(g) limits, State/local expense and voluntary agreement/own no-agreement communication/cooperation paths remain; no blanket deputization, power or immunity. Victim-assistance perpetrator condition is not status-based guilt, cash for every victim or actual crime. Family paragraph (8) remains separately qualified. No actual hiring/bonus/agreement/collection/removal/expenditure or full-package closure.

Senate 90002 provides $4.1 billion for personnel, $2,052,630,000 for bonuses/awards and $855 million for vehicles. Each of those three paragraphs is a fiscal year 2025 appropriation expressly available until September 30, 2029. The separate $5 billion for facilities and checkpoints owned, leased or operated by CBP does not print that phrase, with availability application reserved as question 45 before any borrowed or assumed expiry. Coordinator recruiting/hiring/training restriction applies to (a) funds after October 31, 2028, not immediate/all-funding employment prohibition. Own recruitment/performance/retention and repair/unit purposes, no House/ICE substitution. 90004 $6.168 billion envelope until September 30, 2029 includes its own listed technology/entry-or-exit/initial-UAC-screening/trafficking/commemoration purposes, not separate House earmarks. Southwest/northern tower condition requires same tower both tested and accepted by CBP under own autonomous definition; fund/geographic/authority scope distinct, no actual accuracy or immigration finding. Complete biometric/UAC/TVPRA conditions retained, no every-traveller collection or imported House tattoo/disclosure/withdrawal mechanism. 90007 DHS $10 billion border-support cost reimbursement has own dates/purpose, not an inferred State-only/January-date restriction or actual award. 100053 provides a $750 million FLETC envelope, with at least $285 million for training and at most $465 million for facilities. Training includes newly hired Federal law enforcement personnel employed by DHS and State and local law enforcement agencies operating in support of DHS. Facility purposes include the named maintenance and training equipment. These are not exact House splits. Own stated availability until September 30, 2029 retained. No individual enforcement/child outcome, actual hire/award/data/reimbursement/expenditure or full-package closure.

Senate 100054 fiscal year 2025 $3.33 billion DOJ envelope through September 30, 2029 has separate selected EOIR, Byrne/COPS and incarceration purposes; neither all funds nor House earmarks are assigned to one. EOIR judges/support addresses backlog; not-more-than-800-judges ceiling effective November 1, 2028 is not an actual count, minimum or inferred cut. Paragraph (7) compensation requires felony or at least two misdemeanor convictions in every case, plus one complete entry/proceeding-at-custody/nonimmigrant-status-failure-at-custody alternative, with all listed entity funding exclusions retained. No status/charge shortcut, actual award or State violation. Paragraph (5) located community-violence funding limitation and AG-determined 1373 compliance, and (7)(C) more-than-one-State distribution, print under-this-subsection references with scope reserved as question 46; no settled whole-account or purpose-only application. Complete 1373 own information-purpose/agency boundaries and old 241(i) compensation route retained, not constitutional acceptance, unlimited data/arrest authority, first-ever compensation, or imported old-route conditions. No individual guilt/State disqualification/actual hires/backlog/grant/custody/removal outcome or full-package closure.

Senate 100054(2)/(3) drug/prosecution purposes use the shared $3.33 billion fiscal year 2025 envelope through September 30, 2029, without House earmarks. Own listed matters include unlawful voting; full 611 federal-office/exception/nonapplication predicates remain, no generic alien-guilt or new benefit/voting rule. Separate 100055 DOJ Fund. The Attorney General shall use the Fund amounts for grants to eligible States, State agencies, and units of local government, pursuant to their existing statutory authorities, for any of the following purposes. The paragraph 1 purpose is locating and apprehending aliens who have committed a crime under Federal, State, or local law, in addition to being unlawfully present in the United States. The paragraph 2 purpose is collection and analysis of law enforcement investigative information within the United States to counter gang or other criminal activity. The paragraph 3 purpose is investigating and prosecuting crimes committed by aliens within the United States and drug and human trafficking crimes committed within the United States. The paragraph 4 purpose is court operations related to the prosecution of crimes committed by aliens and drug and human trafficking crimes. The paragraph 5 purpose is temporary criminal detention of aliens. The paragraph 6 purpose is transporting aliens described in paragraph (1) within the United States to locations related to the apprehension, detention, and prosecution of such aliens. The paragraph 7 purpose is vehicle maintenance, logistics, transportation, and other support provided to law enforcement agencies by a State agency to enhance the ability to locate and apprehend aliens who have committed crimes under Federal, State, or local law, in addition to being unlawfully present in the United States. Paragraphs (1) and (7) retain their own additional-crime and unlawful-presence requirements; paragraph (6) retains the paragraph (1) person category, its domestic transport limit and its destination purposes. Those requirements are not imported into the other purposes. Temporary criminal detention is distinct from civil immigration detention. Court paragraph (4) prints no separate within-the-United-States phrase; no neighboring location condition is borrowed. Listed conjunctions report the source categories, not a determination that a particular grant must fund both crime categories. Existing statutory authorities do not create new State arrest/removal powers or establish actual crime/status/expense eligibility. Fiscal year 2025 appropriation is not to exceed $3,500,000,000 ($3.5 billion) until September 30, 2028, with qualified and documented expenses. The Attorney General may provide grants to State agencies and units of local government for their expenditures for completed, ongoing, or new activities determined to be eligible for such grant funding that occurred on or after January 20, 2021. Amounts made available under this section shall be distributed to more than 1 State. No borrowed January 21 or 2029 date, automatic grant, actual crime/status/detention/hiring/spending or full-package closure. Existing question 46 subsection-scope application is unchanged.

Senate 100051(9)/(10) use the additional fiscal year 2025 $2,055,000,000 DHS envelope through September 30, 2029, in accordance with 235(b)(1)/(c), without House earmarks, House's express 212(a)(2)/(3) grounds wording or regardless-of-presence phrase. Complete own screening/designation/asylum/fear/record/requested-review/consultation/detention/exception/protected-status procedures remain. Both AG confidential-information inadmissibility and post-consultation disclosure-prejudice predicates precede discretionary 235(c) removal without further immigration-judge inquiry; further-inquiry and written-submission rules remain. Full criminal/security grounds and conditional waivers are not conviction-only or automatic status classifiers. Full 242(e) limited judicial-review/relief/court/deadline/remedy/inquiry scope and distinct January 2025 State-enforcement/injunction amendments retained. Questions 47/48 stay House application reservations, not new Senate expansion rules. No actual crime/status/waiver/asylum/hearing/review/custody/removal or full-package closure.

Senate 100051(8) and (11) are purposes within the additional $2,055,000,000 fiscal year 2025 appropriation to the Secretary of Homeland Security, available through September 30, 2029. Neither purpose is a separate earmark for the full account, the ICE account or a House child appropriation. Paragraph (8) funds removal operations for specified unaccompanied alien children, but amounts under this paragraph shall only be used for permitting a specified unaccompanied alien child to withdraw the application for admission of the child pursuant to section 235(a)(4). The Secretary of Homeland Security must determine on a case-by-case basis all three specified-child conditions. First, the child has been found by an immigration officer at a land border or port of entry of the United States and is inadmissible under the Immigration and Nationality Act. Second, the child has not been a victim of severe forms of trafficking in persons, and there is no credible evidence that such child is at risk of being trafficked upon return of the child to the child's country of nationality or country of last habitual residence. Third, the child does not have a fear of returning to the child's country of nationality or country of last habitual residence owing to a credible fear of persecution. The paragraph does not print the House express contiguous-or-non-contiguous-country phrase or an independent-decision finding; neither is silently inserted into its definition. The incorporated unaccompanied-alien-child definition requires no lawful immigration status in the United States and not having attained 18 years of age, together with either no parent or legal guardian in the United States or no parent or legal guardian in the United States available to provide care and physical custody. The complete severe-forms-of-trafficking definition is bound with its own sex-trafficking and labor-or-services alternatives, force/fraud/coercion and under-18 distinctions; no label alone determines a child's eligibility. Paragraph (11) funds criminal and gang checks of defined unaccompanied alien children who are 12 years of age and older, including the examination of such unaccompanied alien children for gang-related tattoos and other gang-related markings. It prints no separate encountered-by-CBP condition; the House 70116 encounter condition is not imported. Its age-12 floor belongs to this check purpose, not the paragraph (8) withdrawal definition. Examination funding is not a finding that a child belongs to a gang, has committed a crime or is dangerous. Complete material captured pre-vote 235(a)(4) retains discretionary permission to withdraw and depart immediately, not a mandatory withdrawal or removal order. Complete TVPRA 235/1232 retains its own contiguous-child case-by-case trafficking/fear and independent-decision conditions, discretionary withdrawal/return, safe-return conditions, 48-hour screening and failed-or-undetermined-screen transfer, other-child custody pathway and own notification/72-hour-transfer exceptions. Its removal-proceedings, relief/access-to-counsel, placement, suitability and remaining safeguards retain their own scope. Senate funding does not itself establish their repeal, fulfillment or a universal individual return, protection or counsel outcome. Exact application interaction remains separate question 49; House question 43 is preserved independently.

Senate 100051(5) fingerprint and DNA purposes are within the additional $2,055,000,000 fiscal year 2025 Secretary of Homeland Security account through September 30, 2029. Both purposes share the printed circumstance of aliens and alien children entering the United States without a valid visa. Subparagraph (A) funds collecting fingerprints, in accordance with section 262 and subsections (a)(3) and (b) of section 235 of the Immigration and Nationality Act. Subparagraph (B) separately funds collecting DNA, in accordance with sections 235(d) and 287(b) of that Act. These are funding purposes with their own incorporated authorities, not a determination that every alien or child is subject to every collection power or that funded collection actually occurred. Captured 262(a) concerns an alien now or hereafter in the United States who is fourteen years of age or older, has not been registered and fingerprinted under section 1201(b) or section 30 or 31 of the Alien Registration Act, 1940, and remains in the United States for thirty days or longer. All those conditions are common to its duty to apply for registration and to be fingerprinted before the expiration of such thirty days. Captured 262(b) separately requires a parent or legal guardian to apply for registration of an alien now or hereafter in the United States who is less than fourteen years of age, has not been registered under those named provisions, and remains in the United States for thirty days or longer, before that period expires. That parent/guardian provision prints registration, not the same under-14 fingerprint duty. Whenever an alien attains his fourteenth birthday in the United States, the separate rule requires in-person registration and fingerprinting within thirty days thereafter. Captured 262(c) retains the Attorney General's discretionary nonimmigrant fingerprint waiver on the basis of reciprocity pursuant to prescribed regulations; no actual waiver is inferred. Complete 235(a)(3) concerns inspection of aliens, including crewmen, who apply for or otherwise seek admission, readmission or transit; it does not itself print a fingerprint command. Complete material 235(b)(1)/(2) screening, exceptions, asylum/fear/interview/review/consultation/detention and contiguous-return conditions remain bound, together with the original favorable-admission challenge. January 29, 2025 Public Law 119-1 renumbers that original challenge from (3) to (4) and inserts the distinct State enforcement (3); the captured 2024 wording is not relabeled as an unamended 2025 subsection. Complete 235(d) retains its own belief-based conveyance search, detention/delivery with the alien-crewmember exception, named oath/evidence powers and subpoena-purpose/court-enforcement conditions. Complete 287(b) retains the designated officer/employee oath/evidence scope and its own knowing-or-willful false-evidence/perjury conditions. Neither cited provision expressly names DNA collection. That literal observation does not resolve whether other law, implementation rules or this funding language supports a proposed collection; question 50 reserves the exact DNA authority/application interaction. Question 51 separately reserves the fingerprint-purpose no-valid-visa circumstance alongside the incorporated registration age/prior-registration/duration/waiver paths and inspection procedures. No statutory repeal, guaranteed discretion outcome, universal biometric collection or actual child/parent/status/registration finding is inferred.

Remaining Senate 100051 purposes (1) through (4), (6), (7) and (12) share the additional $2,055,000,000 fiscal year 2025 appropriation to the Secretary of Homeland Security, available through September 30, 2029. They are purposes within that account, not separate full-envelope earmarks or borrowed ICE/House amounts. The paragraph 1 purpose is hiring and training of additional U.S. Customs and Border Protection agents, and the necessary support staff, to carry out immigration enforcement activities. The paragraph 2 purpose is funding for transportation costs and related costs associated with the departure or removal of aliens. The paragraph 3 purpose is funding for the assignment of Department of Homeland Security employees and State officers to carry out immigration enforcement activities pursuant to sections 103(a) and 287(g) of the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1103(a) and 1357(g)). The paragraph 4 purpose is hiring additional staff and investing the necessary resources to enhance screening and vetting of all aliens seeking entry into United States, consistent with section 212 of such Act (8 U.S.C. 1182), or intending to remain in the United States, consistent with section 237 of such Act (8 U.S.C. 1227). The paragraph 6 purpose is transporting and facilitating the return, pursuant to section 235(b)(2)(C) of the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1225(b)(2)(C)), of aliens arriving from contiguous territory. The paragraph 7 purpose is funding for State and local participation in homeland security efforts for purposes of: ending the presence of criminal gangs and criminal organizations throughout the United States; addressing crime and public safety threats; combating human smuggling and trafficking networks throughout the United States; supporting immigration enforcement activities; and providing reimbursement for State and local participation in such efforts. The paragraph 12 purpose is information technology investments to support immigration purposes, including improvements to fee and revenue collections. The entry and intended-remain screening categories retain their own section 212 and section 237 references. The State/local participation list retains all five own purposes, including its own throughout-the-United-States phrases. It does not borrow the reimbursement fund's crime-plus-unlawful-presence category or domestic transport restriction. The general departure/removal transportation purpose prints no separate within-the-United-States phrase. The assignment list retains Department of Homeland Security employees and State officers pursuant to both printed statutory references, not authority for any State employee to exercise all Federal powers. The printed purpose lists do not determine that a particular expenditure must fulfill every listed category. Fee and revenue collection IT is not a new fee, fine or penalty charge. Complete captured 103(a) retains its named agency roles, regulatory/delegation powers, consents and other conditions. In captured 103(a)(10), the Attorney General may authorize a State or local law enforcement officer to perform or exercise any of the powers, privileges, or duties conferred or imposed by this chapter or regulations issued thereunder upon officers or employees of the Service only in the event of the Attorney General's determination that an actual or imminent mass influx of aliens arriving off the coast of the United States, or near a land border, presents urgent circumstances requiring an immediate Federal response, and with the consent of the head of the department, agency, or establishment under whose jurisdiction the individual is serving. The captured event-specific authorization does not establish general unconditioned State power. Previously bound full 287(g) agreement qualifications, training, written powers/duration, Federal direction/supervision, voluntary/communication/cooperation and expense/employment/liability distinctions remain unchanged. Complete captured section 212(a) grounds and remaining operative section 212 authorities retain their own standards, exceptions, discretionary waivers and conditional notice rules, not an every-alien crime finding or guaranteed notice/waiver. January 29, 2025 Public Law 119-1 replaces the original Attorney General references in 212(d)(5) with Secretary of Homeland Security and adds the distinct State enforcement route. Original captured 2024 words are preserved with that amending law, not relabeled as the complete unamended 2025 section. Complete captured section 237 retains distinct deportability grounds, actual conviction/knowledge/timing or other own requirements, exceptions/waivers, special nonimmigrant and SIJ boundaries and conditional administrative stays; screening funding does not determine an individual inadmissible, deportable or criminal. The contiguous-return purpose is pursuant to 235(b)(2)(C). The captured 235(b)(2)(C) return authority concerns an applicant for admission whom the examining immigration officer determines is not clearly and beyond a doubt entitled to be admitted, arriving on land (whether or not at a designated port of arrival) from a foreign territory contiguous to the United States. The Attorney General may return that alien to that territory pending a proceeding under section 1229a. The captured parent exceptions for a crewman, an alien to whom paragraph (1) applies, and a stowaway remain. Discretionary return is not a final removal order or universal cross-border return duty. Complete captured 240 proceedings retain judge/charge/exclusive-procedure exceptions, own representation and evidence/examination limits, burdens, decision/appeal, motion and notice/deadline/stay rules. No guaranteed relief, government-paid counsel or individual hearing/return result is inferred. Other H.R.1 immigration components and separately reserved application questions remain unfinished.

The Senate 90005(b) State Border Security Reinforcement Fund is a distinct DHS fund. Its complete selected operative clauses are retained below. Senate 90005(b) paragraph 1: There is established, in the Department of Homeland Security, a fund to be known as the ``State Border Security Reinforcement Fund.'' Senate 90005(b) paragraph 2: The Secretary of Homeland Security shall use amounts appropriated or otherwise made available for the Fund for grants to eligible States and units of local government for any of the following purposes: Senate 90005(b) purpose A: Construction or installation of a border wall, border fencing or other barrier, or buoys along the southern border of the United States, which may include planning, procurement of materials, and personnel costs related to such construction or installation. Senate 90005(b) purpose B: Any work necessary to prepare the ground at or near land borders to allow construction and maintenance of a border wall or other barrier fencing. Senate 90005(b) purpose C: Detection and interdiction of illicit substances and aliens who have unlawfully entered the United States and have committed a crime under Federal, State, or local law, and transfer or referral of such aliens to the Department of Homeland Security as provided by law. Senate 90005(b) purpose D: Relocation of aliens who are unlawfully present in the United States from small population centers to other domestic locations. Senate 90005(b) paragraph 3: In addition to amounts otherwise available for the purposes described in paragraph (2), there is appropriated for fiscal year 2025, out of any money in the Treasury not otherwise appropriated, to the Department of Homeland Security for the State Border Security Reinforcement Fund established by paragraph (1), $10,000,000,000, to remain available until September 30, 2034, for qualified expenses for such purposes. Senate 90005(b) paragraph 4: The Secretary of Homeland Security may provide grants from the fund established by paragraph (1) to State agencies and units of local governments for expenditures made for completed, ongoing, or new activities, in accordance with law, that occurred on or after January 20, 2021. Senate 90005(b) paragraph 5: Each State desiring to apply for a grant under this subsection shall submit an application to the Secretary containing such information in support of the application as the Secretary may require. The Secretary shall require that each State include in its application the purposes for which the State seeks the funds and a description of how the State plans to allocate the funds. The Secretary shall begin to accept applications not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act. Senate 90005(b) paragraph 6: Nothing in this subsection shall authorize any State or local government to exercise immigration or border security authorities reserved exclusively to the Federal Government under the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1101 et seq.) or the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (6 U.S.C. 101 et seq.). The Federal Emergency Management Agency may use not more than 1 percent of the funds made available under this subsection for the purpose of administering grants provided for in this section. The paragraph (2)(C) alien category retains both unlawful entry and commission of a crime under Federal, State, or local law; those alien predicates do not classify illicit substances. Transfer or referral remains as provided by law. Paragraph (2)(D) instead concerns unlawful presence and relocation from small population centers to other domestic locations; it does not borrow the crime or unlawful-entry predicates from (C), or authorize an international return. Only (A) specifies the southern border; (B) says at or near land borders. The paragraph (2) eligible-State/local-unit grant purpose rule and paragraph (4) discretionary State-agency/local-government expenditure rule remain distinct. The paragraph (5) application obligations name each State; no additional local-government obligation is inferred. The 90-day clause concerns when the Secretary must begin accepting applications, not an applicant deadline or a finding that applications are open. Senate 70201 deduction and reporting gate: There shall be allowed as a deduction an amount equal to the qualified tips received during the taxable year that are included on statements furnished to the individual pursuant to section 6041(d)(3), 6041A(e)(3), 6050W(f)(2), or 6051(a)(18), or reported by the taxpayer on Form 4137 (or successor). (B) Modified adjusted gross income.--For purposes of this paragraph, the term `modified adjusted gross income' means the adjusted gross income of the taxpayer for the taxable year increased by any amount excluded from gross income under section 911, 931, or 933. Selected exact Senate 87001 ORR sponsor-vetting funding and own purpose boundaries follow. Senate 87001 ORR appropriation: (a) Appropriation.--In addition to amounts otherwise available, there is appropriated to the Office of Refugee Resettlement for fiscal year 2025, out of any money in the Treasury not otherwise appropriated, $300,000,000, to remain available until September 30, 2028, for the purposes described in subsection (b). Senate 87001 exclusive funded-purpose boundary: (b) Use of Funds.--The funds made available under subsection (a) may only be used for the Office of Refugee Resettlement to support costs associated with-- Senate 87001 background-check purpose and required contents: (1) background checks on potential sponsors, which shall include-- (A) the name of the potential sponsor and of all adult residents of the potential sponsor's household; (B) the social security number or tax payer identification number of the potential sponsor and of all adult residents of the potential sponsor's household; (C) the date of birth of the potential sponsor and of all adult residents of the potential sponsor's household; (D) the validated location of the residence at which the unaccompanied alien child will be placed; (E) an in-person or virtual interview with, and suitability study concerning, the potential sponsor and all adult residents of the potential sponsor's household; (F) contact information for the potential sponsor and for all adult residents of the potential sponsor's household; and (G) the results of all background and criminal records checks for the potential sponsor and for all adult residents of the potential sponsor's household, which shall include, at a minimum, an investigation of the public records sex offender registry, a public records background check, and a national criminal history check based on fingerprints; Senate 87001 home-study purpose: (2) home studies of potential sponsors of unaccompanied alien children; Senate 87001 child examination and covering purpose: (3) determining whether an unaccompanied alien child poses a danger to self or others by conducting an examination of the unaccompanied alien child for gang-related tattoos and other gang-related markings and covering such tattoos or markings while the child is in the care of the Office of Refugee Resettlement; Senate 87001 data-system purpose: (4) data systems improvement and sharing that supports the health, safety, and well being of unaccompanied alien children by determining the appropriateness of potential sponsors of unaccompanied alien children and of adults residing in the household of the potential sponsor and by assisting with the identification and investigation of child labor exploitation and child trafficking; and Senate 87001 State child-welfare coordination purpose: (5) coordinating and communicating with State child welfare agencies regarding the placement of unaccompanied alien children in such States by the Office of Refugee Resettlement. Senate 87001 own sponsor and child definitions: (c) Definitions.--In this section: (1) Potential sponsor.--The term potential sponsor means an individual or entity who applies for the custody of an unaccompanied alien child. (2) Unaccompanied alien child.--The term unaccompanied alien child has the meaning given such term in section 462(g) of the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (6 U.S.C. 279(g)). Original 279(g) incorporated category boundary: The incorporated unaccompanied alien child category requires all three conditions: has no lawful immigration status in the United States; has not attained 18 years of age; and either there is no parent or legal guardian in the United States, or no parent or legal guardian in the United States is available to provide care and physical custody. Placement means the placement of an unaccompanied alien child in either a detention facility or an alternative to such a facility. Age alone does not establish this category, and availability for care and physical custody is retained. Original 1232(c)(2)-(3) placement and suitability protections: (2) Safe and secure placements (A) Minors in department of health and human services custody Subject to section 279(b)(2) of title 6, an unaccompanied alien child in the custody of the Secretary of Health and Human Services shall be promptly placed in the least restrictive setting that is in the best interest of the child. In making such placements, the Secretary may consider danger to self, danger to the community, and risk of flight. Placement of child trafficking victims may include placement in an Unaccompanied Refugee Minor program, pursuant to section 412(d) of the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1522(d)), if a suitable family member is not available to provide care. A child shall not be placed in a secure facility absent a determination that the child poses a danger to self or others or has been charged with having committed a criminal offense. The placement of a child in a secure facility shall be reviewed, at a minimum, on a monthly basis, in accordance with procedures prescribed by the Secretary, to determine if such placement remains warranted. (B) Aliens transferred from Department of Health and Human Services to Department of Homeland Security custody If a minor described in subparagraph (A) reaches 18 years of age and is transferred to the custody of the Secretary of Homeland Security, the Secretary shall consider placement in the least restrictive setting available after taking into account the alien's danger to self, danger to the community, and risk of flight. Such aliens shall be eligible to participate in alternative to detention programs, utilizing a continuum of alternatives based on the alien's need for supervision, which may include placement of the alien with an individual or an organizational sponsor, or in a supervised group home. (3) Safety and suitability assessments (A) In general Subject to the requirements of subparagraph (B), an unaccompanied alien child may not be placed with a person or entity unless the Secretary of Health and Human Services makes a determination that the proposed custodian is capable of providing for the child's physical and mental well-being. Such determination shall, at a minimum, include verification of the custodian's identity and relationship to the child, if any, as well as an independent finding that the individual has not engaged in any activity that would indicate a potential risk to the child. (B) Home studies Before placing the child with an individual, the Secretary of Health and Human Services shall determine whether a home study is first necessary. A home study shall be conducted for a child who is a victim of a severe form of trafficking in persons, a special needs child with a disability (as defined in section 12102 of title 42), a child who has been a victim of physical or sexual abuse under circumstances that indicate that the child's health or welfare has been significantly harmed or threatened, or a child whose proposed sponsor clearly presents a risk of abuse, maltreatment, exploitation, or trafficking to the child based on all available objective evidence. The Secretary of Health and Human Services shall conduct follow-up services, during the pendency of removal proceedings, on children for whom a home study was conducted and is authorized to conduct follow-up services in cases involving children with mental health or other needs who could benefit from ongoing assistance from a social welfare agency. (C) Access to information Not later than 2 weeks after receiving a request from the Secretary of Health and Human Services, the Secretary of Homeland Security shall provide information necessary to conduct suitability assessments from appropriate Federal, State, and local law enforcement and immigration databases. Senate adds $300 million to ORR for fiscal year 2025, available until September 30, 2028; this is a separate actor/account/date from DHS/ICE funds, not an actual expenditure, placement, screening finding or universal detention mandate. Funds may only support the five printed purpose categories. The background-check purpose shall include all seven items for their own named sponsor/household subjects; retain social security number or tax payer identification number as alternatives, in-person or virtual interview as alternatives, suitability study and all adult residents, and minimum fingerprint-based national criminal history/public-record/sex-offender checks. Do not turn this appropriation into a new universal sponsor citizenship or work-authorized-SSN condition. The child examination purpose has no printed age-12 floor, no CBP-encounter requirement, and covers tattoos or markings while the child is in ORR care; House 70116/70117 conditions are not imported. An examination purpose does not itself establish gang affiliation or danger, and the data-sharing child-labor/trafficking purposes do not establish actual exploitation findings. Potential sponsor expressly includes an individual or entity who applies for custody. The existing full 279 and 1232(c) authorities remain bound with category, placement, suitability, home-study and counsel/advocate protections; this funding is not first-ever placement vetting authority or an implicit repeal of child-protection rules. Exact background-check/use-of-funds conditions are represented as funding-purpose conditions, not a fabricated standalone universal placement deadline or verified practice. Specific protocol, actual placement and compliance/outcome application remain outside this literal candidate. Other H.R.1 component research and the 61 separately reserved application questions remain unfinished.

Selected exact Senate scholarship contributing-taxpayer scope and own-version boundaries follow. Senate own new 25F clause a: (a) Allowance of Credit.--In the case of an individual who is a citizen or resident of the United States (within the meaning of section 7701(a)(9)), there shall be allowed as a credit against the tax imposed by this chapter for the taxable year an amount equal to the aggregate amount of qualified contributions made by the taxpayer during the taxable year. Senate own new 25F clause b: (b) Limitations.-- (1) In general.--The credit allowed under subsection (a) to any taxpayer for any taxable year shall not exceed $1,700. (2) Reduction based on state credit.--The amount allowed as a credit under subsection (a) for a taxable year shall be reduced by the amount allowed as a credit on any State tax return of the taxpayer for qualified contributions made by the taxpayer during the taxable year. Senate own new 25F clause c: (c) Definitions.--For purposes of this section-- (1) Covered state.--The term `covered State' means one of the States, or the District of Columbia, that, for a calendar year, voluntarily elects to participate under this section and to identify scholarship granting organizations in the State, in accordance with subsection (g). (2) Eligible student.--The term `eligible student' means an individual who-- (A) is a member of a household with an income which, for the calendar year prior to the date of the application for a scholarship, is not greater than 300 percent of the area median gross income (as such term is used in section 42), and (B) is eligible to enroll in a public elementary or secondary school. (3) Qualified contribution.--The term `qualified contribution' means a charitable contribution of cash to a scholarship granting organization that uses the contribution to fund scholarships for eligible students solely within the State in which the organization is listed pursuant to subsection (g). (4) Qualified elementary or secondary education expense.--The term `qualified elementary or secondary education expense' means any expense of an eligible student which is described in section 530(b)(3)(A). (5) Scholarship granting organization.--The term `scholarship granting organization' means any organization-- (A) which-- (i) is described in section 501(c)(3) and exempt from tax under section 501(a), and (ii) is not a private foundation, (B) which prevents the co-mingling of qualified contributions with other amounts by maintaining one or more separate accounts exclusively for qualified contributions, (C) which satisfies the requirements of subsection (d), and (D) which is included on the list submitted for the applicable covered State under subsection (g) for the applicable year. Senate own new 25F clause d: (d) Requirements for Scholarship Granting Organizations.-- (1) In general.--An organization meets the requirements of this subsection if-- (A) such organization provides scholarships to 10 or more students who do not all attend the same school, (B) such organization spends not less than 90 percent of the income of the organization on scholarships for eligible students, (C) such organization does not provide scholarships for any expenses other than qualified elementary or secondary education expenses, (D) such organization provides a scholarship to eligible students with a priority for-- (i) students awarded a scholarship the previous school year, and (ii) after application of clause (i), any eligible students who have a sibling who was awarded a scholarship from such organization, (E) such organization does not earmark or set aside contributions for scholarships on behalf of any particular student, and (F) such organization-- (i) verifies the annual household income and family size of eligible students who apply for scholarships to ensure such students meet the requirement of subsection (c)(2)(A), and (ii) limits the awarding of scholarships to eligible students who are a member of a household for which the income does not exceed the amount established under subsection (c)(2)(A). (2) Prohibition on self-dealing.-- (A) In general.--A scholarship granting organization may not award a scholarship to any disqualified person. (B) Disqualified person.--For purposes of this paragraph, a disqualified person shall be determined pursuant to rules similar to the rules of section 4946. Senate own new 25F clause e: (e) Denial of Double Benefit.--Any qualified contribution for which a credit is allowed under this section shall not be taken into account as a charitable contribution for purposes of section 170. Senate own new 25F clause f: (f) Carryforward of Unused Credit.-- (1) In general.--If the credit allowable under subsection (a) for any taxable year exceeds the limitation imposed by section 26(a) for such taxable year reduced by the sum of the credits allowable under this subpart (other than this section, section 23, and section 25D), such excess shall be carried to the succeeding taxable year and added to the credit allowable under subsection (a) for such taxable year. (2) Limitation.--No credit may be carried forward under this subsection to any taxable year following the fifth taxable year after the taxable year in which the credit arose. For purposes of the preceding sentence, credits shall be treated as used on a first-in first-out basis. Senate own new 25F clause g: (g) State List of Scholarship Granting Organizations.-- (1) List.-- (A) In general.--Not later than January 1 of each calendar year (or, with respect to the first calendar year for which this section applies, as early as practicable), a State that voluntarily elects to participate under this section shall provide to the Secretary a list of the scholarship granting organizations that meet the requirements described in subsection (c)(5) and are located in the State. (B) Process.--The election under this paragraph shall be made by the Governor of the State or by such other individual, agency, or entity as is designated under State law to make such elections on behalf of the State with respect to Federal tax benefits. (2) Certification.--Each list submitted under paragraph (1) shall include a certification that the individual, agency, or entity submitting such list on behalf of the State has the authority to perform this function. Senate own new 25F clause h: (h) Regulations and Guidance.--The Secretary shall issue such regulations or other guidance as the Secretary determines necessary to carry out the purposes of this section, including regulations or other guidance-- (1) providing for enforcement of the requirements under subsections (d) and (g), and (2) with respect to recordkeeping or information reporting for purposes of administering the requirements of this section.. Senate separate scholarship income exclusion: (b) Exclusion From Gross Income for Scholarships for Qualified Elementary or Secondary Education Expenses of Eligible Students.-- (1) In general.--Part III of subchapter B of chapter 1 is amended by inserting before section 140 the following new section: SEC. 139K. SCHOLARSHIPS FOR QUALIFIED ELEMENTARY OR SECONDARY EDUCATION EXPENSES OF ELIGIBLE STUDENTS. (a) In General.--In the case of an individual, gross income shall not include any amounts provided to such individual or any dependent of such individual pursuant to a scholarship for qualified elementary or secondary education expenses of an eligible student which is provided by a scholarship granting organization. (b) Definitions.--In this section, the terms `qualified elementary or secondary education expense', `eligible student', and `scholarship granting organization' have the same meaning given such terms under section 25F(c).. (2) Conforming amendment.--The table of sections for part III of subchapter B of chapter 1 is amended by inserting before the item relating to section 140 the following new item: Sec. 139K. Scholarships for qualified elementary or secondary education expenses of eligible students.. Senate own applicability dates: (c) Effective Date.-- (1) In general.--Except as otherwise provided in this subsection, the amendments made by this section shall apply to taxable years ending after December 31, 2026. (2) Exclusion from gross income.--The amendments made by subsection (b) shall apply to amounts received after December 31, 2026, in taxable years ending after such date. Original printed geographic reference: (9) United States The term "United States" when used in a geographical sense includes only the States and the District of Columbia. Original education-expense reference and definitions: (3) Qualified elementary and secondary education expenses (A) In general The term "qualified elementary and secondary education expenses" means— (i) expenses for tuition, fees, academic tutoring, special needs services in the case of a special needs beneficiary, books, supplies, and other equipment which are incurred in connection with the enrollment or attendance of the designated beneficiary of the trust as an elementary or secondary school student at a public, private, or religious school, (ii) expenses for room and board, uniforms, transportation, and supplementary items and services (including extended day programs) which are required or provided by a public, private, or religious school in connection with such enrollment or attendance, and (iii) expenses for the purchase of any computer technology or equipment or Internet access and related services, if such technology, equipment, or services are to be used by the beneficiary and the beneficiary's family during any of the years the beneficiary is in school. Clause (iii) shall not include expenses for computer software designed for sports, games, or hobbies unless the software is predominantly educational in nature. (B) School The term "school" means any school which provides elementary education or secondary education (kindergarten through grade 12), as determined under State law. (C) Computer technology or equipment The term "computer technology or equipment" means computer software (as defined by section 197(e)(3)(B)), computer or peripheral equipment (as defined by section 168(i)(2)(B)), and fiber optic cable related to computer use.
